I farm 14 mu under a wheat-maize rotation, so I will split the same land across the two seasons rather than split the area between different plots. I have 25 years of experience and well irrigation, so I will manage for stable output instead of taking big risks. For wheat, I will use improved seed, moderate-high fertilizer, several irrigations, and rotary tillage because that fits my land size and labor better than deep ploughing every season. For maize, I will use hybrid seed because I care about yield, then give enough nitrogen, balanced phosphorus and potassium, and fewer irrigations than wheat since summer rain helps. I will keep pesticide use controlled but not excessive, aiming to prevent the common field problems without spending more than needed. My goal this year is steady grain production and reliable returns for the household, not the highest possible yield with the highest possible cost.
